newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIEGEST - Ireland, February 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIEGEST - Ireland, February 26.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Wednesday.
- Consumers and borrowers can look forward to another good year with little threat of higher inflation on interest rates.
- Irish farmers want the government to pay them 50 million Irish pounds compensation because the economy is booming.
- Tough new penalties ranging from five years to life imprisonment for syringe attacks are spelled out in new proposed legislation to be published on Wednesday by Justice Minister Nora Owen.
- The Irish government on Tuesday agreed a major change to the Organisation of Working Times Bill - commonly known as the 48-hour Bill.
- Ulster bank, the country's third largest banking group has announced a 13 percent rise in its pre-tax profits to a record 135 million sterling for 1996. IRISH TIMES
- The rate of inflation has fallen to its lowest in almost four years but the Irish Central bank has sent a clear signal that it will not allow an early reduction in interest rates.
- Thousands of parents face a 21 percent rise in child-care costs because crches and child-minding services say the Revenue Commissioners will impose VAT on them for the first time.
- The parents of a baby born without arms or legs on Tuesday launched an appeal to raise 250,000 Irish pounds to enable her to lead a semi-independent life.

- As the build-up of dead animals continues on Irish farms at a rate of more than 250 a day, meetings are to be held in an attempt to resolve the issues which have led to the carcasses not being collected since last Friday.
- The minister for Enterprise and Employment Richard Bruton has requested a further meeting with the U.S. Chamber of Commerce to discuss its concerns about the Organisation of Working Time Bill.
- Motorists will be hit with another five percent hike in the cost of car insurance before the end of the year.
- Thousands of jobs could be lost in the next few months because of the Irish Central bank's failure to cut interest rates on Tuesday when it issued its monetary policy statement for 1997.
- Citing the higher incidence of BSE in the Republic of Ireland, the British government on Tuesday asked the European Commission to relax the ban on beef exports from Northern Ireland.
- An international dimension to any new inquiry into the events of Bloody Sunday should be considered, the Irish Prime Minister John Bruton told parliament on Tuesday.
- Jerymn Investments Properties is to seek a listing on the Irish Stock Exchange and expects to be trading there within a matter of weeks.
